notes: POC focus: Dedicated capacity evaluation for customer-facing assistant and internal KB search. Key customer constraints: strict data residency for EU customers (subset of traffic), SSO/SAML for internal users, audit logs retention 1 year. Workload details: multi-turn chat + contextual retrieval. Typical request: user prompt ~200-300 tokens + retrieved context ~800 tokens; expected response ~300-600 tokens. Targets: p95 latency <= 250ms for short-turn responses (<256 tokens), p99 < 600ms for full responses; throughput target 400-600 req/s sustained during business hours, ability to absorb 2x peak bursts for 10 minutes. Cost sensitivity: moderate — will trade some cost for guaranteed latency but want optimization suggestions (quantization, batching windows). Model preference: open-vendor family (Llama-variant) but open to Redwood-verified tuned variants. Routing/fallback: must have warm fallback to smaller model variant and regional fallback (NA <-> EU) for outage tolerance. POC plan: run representative prompt suite (50 canonical dialogs + 200 retrieval/rerank queries) across 8 A100-equivalent GPUs, continuous 72-hour soak with steady-state 450 rps, scheduled spike episodes (10m @ 1200 rps x6), collect traces and token-level cost. Metrics to deliver: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, effective batching size, per-route cost breakdown. Security notes: customer requires KMS integration for key management; asking about HSM options and audit log export cadence. Legal: initial redlines around data-processing addendum and cross-border transfer; legal loop involved but not blocking POC. Next: SE to spin up Dedicated POC, deliver kube-level sizing suggestion (estimate: 8x A100 or 12x A40 depending on quantization), run soak tests week of 2025-12-15, then SLA negotiation week of 2026-01-05.
